features.name: Mechanics index
features.mustUnderstand: Table-of-contents note linking to every mechanics page (plus a Known Drift table of copy/code mismatches); it is not itself a feature, just the index.
features.evidence: Everything the player does, read out of the engine rather than out of the old design doc.

features.name: ARM: HALT trap
features.mustUnderstand: An ARM: HALT trap forfeits your entire next turn the instant your signal walks into it, so treat a halt-dominant opponent as a scan-first job before pushing forward blindly.
features.evidence: Plant a halt trap on open junctions on the enemy board. When their signal claims the node, **they lose a full turn**.

features.name: ARM: SIPHON trap
features.mustUnderstand: An ARM: SIPHON trap does not cost you a turn, it steals 2 to 4 RAM from your next turn and hands it to whoever planted it, converting their lead directly into their resources.
features.evidence: Plant a siphon trap on open junctions on the enemy board. When it fires, RAM **drains from their next turn into yours**.

features.name: ATTACK program
features.mustUnderstand: ATTACK is your only program that touches the enemy's board at all, costs 1 RAM, and can be cast once per turn, so it is the sole channel for interfering with the intrusion's progress.
features.evidence: The only program that reaches the **enemy** board. 1 RAM, once per turn.

features.name: Augment drafts
features.mustUnderstand: Clearing a ticket offers a choice of three augments and a clean day can bank three picks, so which tickets you clear, and how cleanly, directly controls how fast you build your kit.
features.evidence: One draft per **cleared ticket**. Three tickets a day, so a clean day banks three picks.

features.name: CHEAP SHOT
features.mustUnderstand: Your first ATTACK cast each dive is free, so opening with a REDIRECT costs nothing and converts straight into extra rotations.
features.evidence: Your first ATTACK each dive costs 0 RAM.

features.name: CLAMP DRIVER
features.mustUnderstand: Drafting CLAMP DRIVER unlocks LOCK as a DEFEND mode, freezing chosen junctions against both rotation and redirect for two rounds, though you must still switch to it in LOADOUT.CFG to use it.
features.evidence: DEFEND config: freeze junctions for 2 rounds against rotation and redirects.

features.name: CLEAN RUN
features.mustUnderstand: Winning a dive without billing any Neural Strain banks a free random patch piece, and even a trap-free win that only misses by going to the round cap still pays a 15 credit consolation.
features.evidence: Win a dive with zero strain billed and bank one random patch piece. A trap-free win that only misses at the round cap pays 15 credits instead.

features.name: DARKNET RATE
features.mustUnderstand: DARKNET RATE cuts the price of a blind darknet pull by 15 percent, but the roll still stays blind and no other purchase gets cheaper.
features.evidence: Dark web patch piece pulls cost 15 percent less. The vendor still only takes credits and the roll stays blind.

features.name: DEEP SIPHON
features.mustUnderstand: DEEP SIPHON adds 1 extra RAM to every siphon trap you spring, stacking with your ATTACK tier so a tier 3 siphon can move 5 RAM at once.
features.evidence: Your siphon traps steal 1 extra RAM.

features.name: ECHO TAP
features.mustUnderstand: ECHO TAP pays you 2 RAM on your next turn whenever any of your traps fires, turning a trap-heavy build from pure denial into a RAM engine.
features.evidence: Whenever one of your traps fires, gain 2 RAM on your next turn.

features.name: FIRST FAULT
features.mustUnderstand: FIRST FAULT forgives the Neural Strain bill for the first enemy trap that hits you each dive, but it never undoes the forfeited turn or drained RAM, only the strain cost.
features.evidence: The first trap that fires on you each dive bills zero Neural Strain. Every trap after that costs full.

features.name: HALT DRIVER
features.mustUnderstand: Drafting HALT DRIVER unlocks ARM: HALT as a selectable ATTACK mode, but you still have to switch to it in LOADOUT.CFG before you can plant halt traps.
features.evidence: ATTACK config: plant halt traps. A sprung trap costs the intrusion its whole next turn.

features.name: HOT BOOT
features.mustUnderstand: HOT BOOT gives you 1 extra RAM on the first turn of every dive, buying the same kind of opening tempo as a free first attack.
features.evidence: Start every dive with +1 RAM on your first turn.

features.name: JAM ANCHOR
features.mustUnderstand: JAM ANCHOR makes every REDIRECT you cast also freeze the junction it twists, so one 1 RAM cast both cuts their route and locks it, without spending a DEFEND.
features.evidence: Your REDIRECT also freezes the junction it twists through the reply and into your next turn. Nothing rotates or redirects it back while it holds.

features.name: LONG ARMS
features.mustUnderstand: LONG ARMS doubles your working reach from 2 to 4 steps ahead of your built ground for both rotating and placing pieces, letting you stage a longer chain before flipping it for a bigger cascade payout.
features.evidence: Rotate open junctions up to 4 steps from your territory instead of 2, and place patch pieces just as far. Bigger setups, bigger cascades.

features.name: OVERTIME CLAUSE
features.mustUnderstand: OVERTIME CLAUSE raises what a round-cap win pays from 50 percent of the ticket to 75 percent, so it is worth the most exactly when a run is already going badly.
features.evidence: Cap wins pay 75 percent of the ticket instead of 50. The client eats every hour past the deadline, not half.

features.name: SIPHON DRIVER
features.mustUnderstand: Drafting SIPHON DRIVER unlocks ARM: SIPHON as a selectable ATTACK mode, stealing more RAM as your ATTACK tier rises.
features.evidence: ATTACK config: plant siphon traps. A sprung trap drains RAM from its next turn into yours, more at higher ATTACK tiers, and more again when you are the one springing it.

features.name: SPLICE REFUND
features.mustUnderstand: SPLICE REFUND gives back the full 4 RAM cost of placing a patch piece the instant it lands, though the piece itself still leaves your pouch, and the draft will not offer it if your pouch is currently empty.
features.evidence: Placing a patch piece refunds its full RAM cost the instant it lands. The pouch still spends the piece itself.

features.name: SWEEP CREDIT
features.mustUnderstand: SWEEP CREDIT refunds 1 RAM for every trap a single PURGE cast defuses, up to 3, which can make clearing a trap-heavy board RAM positive instead of a pure cost.
features.evidence: PURGE refunds 1 RAM per trap it defuses, up to 3 per cast.

features.name: TAP LINE
features.mustUnderstand: TAP LINE makes SCAN also reveal the intrusion's planned route to its goal for 2 rounds, telling you which junction to redirect for maximum damage instead of guessing.
features.evidence: SCAN also traces the intrusion's planned route to the core, visible for 2 rounds.

features.name: TRIPWIRE
features.mustUnderstand: TRIPWIRE adds a 3 RAM drain on top of the forfeited turn a halt trap already costs its victim, stacking a resource hit onto the tempo hit.
features.evidence: Your halt traps also burn 3 RAM off the victim's next active turn.

features.name: WARD DRIVER
features.mustUnderstand: Drafting WARD DRIVER unlocks WARD as a DEFEND mode, the only defensive mode that prevents traps and redirects before they happen rather than answering them after.
features.evidence: DEFEND config: ward an area so no new traps can land in it, and REDIRECT cannot touch anything inside it either, for the full duration on both sides.

features.name: Augments: configs vs boosts
features.mustUnderstand: Augments split into configs, which unlock a new mode on ATTACK or DEFEND without switching you to it, and boosts, which quietly change a rule, and three boosts will not even be offered until you own the config they depend on.
features.evidence: Two kinds. Configs unlock a mode on a program; boosts change a rule.

features.name: Boost bays
features.mustUnderstand: You can only carry 3 boost augments at once, buyable up to 5 at night, but configs never count against that cap, so unlocking every mode never costs you a bay slot.
features.evidence: Bays hold **boosts only**. Configs are exempt from the cap, so unlocking all four modes never costs you a bay.

features.name: Built ground never un-makes
features.mustUnderstand: Once a node lights for the first time it stays permanently built and keeps your reach and cascade progress even after the enemy later cuts its power dark, so a redirect against you costs tempo, never your setup. Not in MECHANIC_INVENTORY under its own id; this is the silent-gap class.
features.evidence: Progress is reversible in throughput and never in construction.

features.name: Cascades and surge
features.mustUnderstand: Lighting three or more nodes in one settle banks RAM into your next turn, six or more shatters every enemy lock on the board, and ten or more also destroys one armed enemy trap, so holding a long chain and releasing it together beats lighting nodes one at a time.
features.evidence: Hold a long chain aligned behind one unturned junction, then flip that junction and light all of it at once.

features.name: Credits
features.mustUnderstand: Credits are earned only by clearing tickets and can only be spent at night on patches, boost bays or a darknet pull, and none of it carries over between runs.
features.evidence: The run currency. Earned by clearing tickets, spent at night.

features.name: Losing a dive is not losing the run
features.mustUnderstand: Losing a single dive does not end the run by itself, it only costs that ticket's pay; the run only ends when Neural Strain hits zero, so a bad dive is recoverable but running your strain to zero is not.
features.evidence: There is no life counter, no continues, no revives, and no mid-run checkpoint. A run either reaches day 10 or it ends.

features.name: DEFEND program
features.mustUnderstand: DEFEND only ever acts on your own board, costs 1 RAM, and can be cast once per turn, covering every way you answer an enemy trap, lock threat or ward gap.
features.evidence: Acts on **your own** board. 1 RAM, once per turn.

features.name: Difficulty dials
features.mustUnderstand: Internal AI tuning dials (horizon, focus, greed) that set opponent behaviour by day; the player never reads these numbers directly, only their downstream effect on how the machine plays.
features.evidence: Three knobs govern how hard the machine is. Only two of them are load-bearing.

features.name: Economy overview
features.mustUnderstand: Structural recap of RAM, credits and Neural Strain as three currencies on three clocks; each is already covered individually by its own note, this adds no new fact.
features.evidence: Three currencies, on three different clocks.

features.name: Job pay and cap-win halving
features.mustUnderstand: Ticket pay rises with job tier, but a round-cap win halves that pay, so finishing messily is not just a strain cost, it is a pay cut too.
features.evidence: 40 + 25 * tier

features.name: LOCK mode
features.mustUnderstand: LOCK freezes chosen junctions against both rotation and redirect for 2 rounds, but it only blocks the other side, never your own, and a SURGE-tier cascade of 6 or more nodes shatters every enemy lock on that board at once.
features.evidence: Freeze junctions for **2 rounds** (`LOCK_ROUNDS`). Nothing rotates or redirects them.

features.name: Neural Strain
features.mustUnderstand: Neural Strain is the run's shared health bar, charged only on a win and only for how untidily it was won, so a perfectly clean dive bills exactly zero and a loss bills nothing at all.
features.evidence: The run's health bar. It is the only thing that ends a run early.

features.name: Opponent AI internals
features.mustUnderstand: AI internals (the cutScore weighting formula, replan counts, stance selection) the player never sees directly; the player-visible half of this note, the one-beat telegraph, is covered separately under telegraph.
features.evidence: The intrusion is a scripted opponent, not a search.

features.name: Patch pieces
features.mustUnderstand: A patch piece fills a slag cell within reach for 4 RAM, once per turn, and its orientation is permanent the instant it is placed, so it can never be rotated later; fit it to the gap you actually need.
features.evidence: Single-use shaped fills. A piece is a **4-bit arm mask with its orientation baked in**: it is never rotatable, in hand or on the board.

features.name: Player character sheet
features.mustUnderstand: Narrative character sheet whose mechanical table just restates strain, RAM, skills, inventory and credits, each already covered by its own note.
features.evidence: The son. Unnamed, never pictured, never speaks in the third person.

features.name: Player inventory overview
features.mustUnderstand: Recap of the pouch, boost bays and kit as three capped containers; each is already covered individually by its own note.
features.evidence: Three containers, all capped, all emptied at run end.

features.name: Player metrics reference
features.mustUnderstand: Reference table aggregating metrics (RAM, par, strain, etc.) that are each already covered by their own mechanic notes; no new fact of its own.
features.evidence: Every number attached to the player, and where it lives.

features.name: Player skills overview
features.mustUnderstand: Recap of programs, tiers and modes as the three axes of power; already covered individually by the-kit, program-tiers and augments.
features.evidence: The skill system, such as it is. There are no skill trees, no XP and no levels.

features.name: Program tiers
features.mustUnderstand: Each of your three programs tiers independently up to 3, bought one per night, and a higher tier buys more targets per cast (and more RAM stolen for siphon), so which program you tier first is a real build decision.
features.evidence: Width is targets per cast: nodes redirected, traps planted, traps cleared, locks placed.

features.name: PURGE mode
features.mustUnderstand: PURGE can only disarm traps that SCAN has already revealed, so scanning before you push into unscanned ground is the prerequisite half of the counter, not an optional extra.
features.evidence: Disarm revealed traps on your own board. 1, 2 or 3 per cast by `DEFEND_WIDTH`.

features.name: RAM as the action budget
features.mustUnderstand: RAM is a hard per-turn spending limit on rotations, casts and placements, starting at 5 and raisable to 9, so you cannot do everything you can see in one turn and have to choose.
features.evidence: The per-turn action budget. RAM is what makes the duel a game of choices rather than a puzzle with one answer.

features.name: RAM carry
features.mustUnderstand: Up to 2 unspent RAM carries into your next turn rather than being lost, so ending a turn a little short is not automatically wasted, but the carry is capped.
features.evidence: carryCap = 2

features.name: Reach and placement
features.mustUnderstand: You may rotate or place a piece up to 2 steps beyond your built ground (4 with LONG ARMS) without lighting it, which is exactly what lets you stage a chain before flipping it for a cascade.
features.evidence: Reach is how far ahead of your built ground you are allowed to work.

features.name: REDIRECT mode
features.mustUnderstand: REDIRECT costs you 1 RAM but can cost the enemy up to 3 RAM to undo on the common elbow and tee junctions, and it instantly resolves their board, so a well aimed twist is cheap leverage but a careless one can hand them the win.
features.evidence: Twist enemy or open junctions a quarter turn, **anywhere on the board, no reach limit**. Cuts power to everything downstream.

features.name: Rotation
features.mustUnderstand: Rotation only ever turns one quarter-turn forward with no shortcut back, and undoing an elbow or tee the enemy twisted costs 3 RAM against the 1 RAM it cost them to twist, so a stray enemy redirect is expensive to fix.
features.evidence: The only movement verb. You twist a junction a quarter turn so its arms line up and signal flows further.

features.name: Route cost and par
features.mustUnderstand: Par is a rotation budget fixed the moment the board is generated, and only your own manual rotations, not program twists or patch placements, count against it, with every rotation past par billing 2 Neural Strain on a win.
features.evidence: One function prices the entire game.

features.name: SCAN program
features.mustUnderstand: SCAN reveals every armed trap within its range on your own board permanently for 1 RAM, and it is the only way to see a trap before PURGE can remove it.
features.evidence: Information. 1 RAM, once per turn, acts on your own board.

features.name: Scoring and lifetime stats
features.mustUnderstand: Describes a persistent lifetime record window rather than a score; informational framing only, it does not change how to play any given dive.
features.evidence: There is no score. Nothing ranks the player and nothing is optimized for points.

features.name: Split boards
features.mustUnderstand: Each side plays on a completely separate grid, so the enemy can never physically occupy your board; only their traps and redirects reach across, which is why defending means answering interference rather than holding ground. Not in MECHANIC_INVENTORY under its own id; this is the silent-gap class.
features.evidence: The enemy is never on your board.

features.name: The board (generation)
features.mustUnderstand: Board generation and fairness constants (rejection sampling, MAX_OPENING_BUILT, headStart compensation) are generator internals the player never reads, the same class as isFrontier; the visible cell kinds are self-evident from the board art.
features.evidence: Each side's grid is generated from the run seed, then rejection-sampled until it is fair.

features.name: The darknet
features.mustUnderstand: A darknet pull sells one patch piece of unknown shape, priced higher each day, so you pay before you know what you are getting.
features.evidence: The gray market. One blind [[patch-pieces|patch piece]], priced by day.

features.name: The duel overview
features.mustUnderstand: Top-level overview synthesizing mechanics that are each covered individually elsewhere (rotation, RAM, attack, defend, cascade, win conditions); useful framing, not a new fact.
features.evidence: The duel is the combat system. Every dive into a customer's device is one duel against one intrusion.

features.name: The kit's counter triangle
features.mustUnderstand: The six modes form a closed counter loop rather than a power ladder: a big cascade shatters locks, scan then purge answers traps, and lock or ward stops redirect, so every telegraphed threat has a castable answer during its wind-up. Not in MECHANIC_INVENTORY under its own id; this is the silent-gap class.
features.evidence: Modes answer each other rather than laddering:

features.name: The night shop
features.mustUnderstand: Closing a day gives one free upgrade pick (RAM or a program tier) plus a shop where credits buy strain relief, a boost bay, or a darknet pull, and you can freely change your free pick while still shopping the rest.
features.evidence: Day close. One free pick, plus anything you can afford.

features.name: The pouch
features.mustUnderstand: Your pouch holds up to 5 patch pieces as fixed shapes, not a simple count, and because a piece can never be rotated to fit, which specific shapes you are carrying matters as much as how many you have.
features.evidence: The pouch is a list of 4-bit arm masks, not a count. Which shapes you hold matters as much as how many, because a piece cannot be rotated to fit.

features.name: The round cap
features.mustUnderstand: If a dive runs past 25 rounds it ends on a route-cost tiebreak instead of a goal, and even winning that way costs an extra 10 Neural Strain and pays only half the ticket.
features.evidence: A cap win is a **messy win**. It costs 10 extra [[neural-strain]] and pays half the ticket, or 75% with [[overtime-clause]].

features.name: Traps and telegraphs
features.mustUnderstand: Every enemy move the machine is about to make is telegraphed one beat ahead and is always answerable in that window, so watching the highlighted aim before it lands is how you get a real chance to counter it.
features.evidence: Interference comes in two forms: a mine you walk into later, and a move you can see coming one beat early.

features.name: The one undo
features.mustUnderstand: You get exactly one undo per turn, armed by a rotation or a placement and spent by any cast, and taking it back does not un-spring a trap it triggered, so undo cannot be used to safely probe for mines. Not in MECHANIC_INVENTORY under its own id; this is the silent-gap class.
features.evidence: Touch-move is the texture of the game. The undo is a fix for a misread, never a tool for exploring the board.

features.name: WARD mode
features.mustUnderstand: WARD prevents new traps from landing and blocks REDIRECT entirely inside its radius for 2 rounds, making it the only defensive mode that acts before a threat exists rather than after.
features.evidence: Ward a junction and everything within a Manhattan radius of it for **2 rounds** (`WARD_ROUNDS`).

features.name: Win conditions
features.mustUnderstand: A dive can only end three ways: your live signal reaches a goal cell, the round cap hits and whoever is closer on route cost wins messily, or (tutorial only) the scripted seal, so a comfortable-looking lead can still be overtaken before you actually touch the goal. Not in MECHANIC_INVENTORY under its own id beyond the turnCap half; this is the silent-gap class.
features.evidence: Three outcomes. That is the complete list.

features.name: Game controls reference
features.mustUnderstand: Control-scheme reference for mechanics already covered elsewhere (rotate, cast, place); the one genuinely new fact here, the single per-turn undo, is captured under oneUndo instead.
features.evidence: **Mouse-driven throughout.** There is no keyboard control scheme, no gamepad support, and no documented shortcut set.

features.name: KP/OS shell
features.mustUnderstand: Interface/art-direction shell (windows, CRT glass, themes); presentation design, not a mechanic to learn.
features.evidence: The shop terminal's retro pixel desktop. **The game does not have an interface. The interface is the game.**

features.name: Music and sound design
features.mustUnderstand: Audio engine and sound design (sfxr palette, buses, stingers); not a gameplay mechanic.
features.evidence: An **sfxr preset palette rendered to buffers on demand**, plus a small additive synth for stingers, plus a music manager for the generated beds.

features.name: Player options menu
features.mustUnderstand: Settings menu (audio, appearance, accessibility); does not affect how to play a dive.
features.evidence: A short list, deliberately. Everything here is either accessibility or taste.

features.name: Title, boot and save slots
features.mustUnderstand: There is no title screen, only a boot sequence into login with three deletable save slots, and each slot tracks its own teaching progress, so a fresh slot is taught everything again from scratch.
features.evidence: Three save slots. Each is a separate save; each can be **deleted** from the login screen.

features.name: BACKROOM.LCK
features.mustUnderstand: Day 10 replaces the whole job board with one screen and one button, no tickets and no shop, so the interface itself announces that the finale day works differently before any copy explains it.
features.evidence: One screen, one button. No tickets, no shop, no choice about what to do next.

features.name: DAD.LOG window
features.mustUnderstand: Presentation of the narrative archive reader (tabs, recovery meter, damaged segments); no gameplay mechanic.
features.evidence: The read-only archive reader over DAD.VOL. Integrated 2026-07-29.

features.name: DARKNET.LNK window
features.mustUnderstand: Buying a dark pull is a four-step ritual, dial, price, buy, blind reveal, and none of those steps let you see the shape before you commit the credits.
features.evidence: The gray-market CLI. Night phase only.

features.name: DIVE.EXE HUD
features.mustUnderstand: HUD layout for the duel screen (RAM, par, round, telegraph); the elements it lists are mechanics already covered by their own entries.
features.evidence: Full-screen

features.name: INBOX / job board
features.mustUnderstand: Three tickets sit on the board at once, takeable in any order, each showing a threat tier and an honest dominant-mode tell, so which ticket you take first is a real decision made before any RAM or strain is spent.
features.evidence: **Three tickets**, takeable in any order.

features.name: LEDGER.LOG window
features.mustUnderstand: Presentation of the lifetime stats record as an accounting terminal; already rejected as informational only under scoring-and-lifetime-stats.
features.evidence: The accounting terminal. There is no score; there are books.

features.name: LOADOUT.CFG window
features.mustUnderstand: LOADOUT.CFG is where you actually switch a program's active mode and see live tier numbers before a dive, and it floats free of the job board with its own DIVE button, so configuring is optional and never blocks diving.
features.evidence: **Attack and defend mode buttons**, locked until the matching config [[augments|augment]] is drafted.

features.name: MANUAL.TXT window
features.mustUnderstand: MANUAL.TXT is a five-tab reference generated live from the same constants the game reducers read, so it can be opened any time a rule or a specific augment's effect needs looking up.
features.evidence: The reference. Five tabs, page-flip navigation: **DIVE · KIT · PATCHES · AUGMENTS · BAYS**.

features.name: NIGHT.SYS window
features.mustUnderstand: Choosing your free night pick does not end the night, so you can keep shopping and even change the pick, because the pick and the purchases trade against each other and you should see both before committing.
features.evidence: `chooseUpgrade` sets the pick **without ending the night**; `closeNight` commits and refuses without a pick.

features.name: REPAIR.LOG window
features.mustUnderstand: The post-dive result reads as a transaction, credited, billed, recovered, and it also carries the augment draft and any boost swap, so this one screen is where you learn why a win cost what it cost and pick your next upgrade.
features.evidence: **CREDITED · BILLED · RECOVERED.** Money in, [[neural-strain|strain]] out, [[patch-pieces|pieces]] recovered.

features.name: SHOPFRONT.EXE window
features.mustUnderstand: Explains why one retitling window serves five different story screens; a UI/window-management decision, not a gameplay mechanic.
features.evidence: **The flow window.** The only window whose title changes with its contents, via `windowTitle()`.

features.name: SOLDER.BAY window
features.mustUnderstand: Welding two patch pieces makes their union, legal only when the result is strictly bigger than both inputs, and the bench shows this by making illegal partners physically undraggable rather than letting you try and fail.
features.evidence: PICK A PARTNER. THE WELD MUST OUTGROW BOTH.

features.name: Teaching index
features.mustUnderstand: Index of the teaching system's own documentation; describes how the game teaches, not something the player must understand to play.
features.evidence: How the player learns the game. Owned by the [[tutorial-agent]], enforced by a build-failing test.

features.name: Coachmarks (the mechanism)
features.mustUnderstand: Describes the coachmark delivery mechanism itself (order, triggers, limits); dev-facing teaching infrastructure, not a player mechanic. The mechanics it lists as taught are already covered under their own entries.
features.evidence: One-time callouts. **A coachmark is a rule you need once.**

features.name: Mechanic coverage bookkeeping
features.mustUnderstand: The inventory and its coverage bookkeeping (taught/waived/planned/retired); meta-documentation about teaching, not a mechanic itself.
features.evidence: The inventory of everything a player must understand, and how each one is covered.

features.name: Placement bias order
features.mustUnderstand: Craft rule for choosing how to teach something (UI over tip over coachmark over manual over scene); process guidance for building the teaching system, not a player mechanic.
features.evidence: The most reusable thing the teaching ledger contains. **Five tiers, and you take the lowest one that works.**

features.name: Standing lessons
features.mustUnderstand: Process lessons extracted from cycle retrospectives for whoever builds the teaching system; not player-facing.
features.evidence: Craft rules extracted from thirteen dated cycle retrospectives in `tutorial/ledger.md`.

features.name: Teaching system rules
features.mustUnderstand: The teaching engine's own rules (eligibility, anchoring, single-winner precedence, limits); infrastructure that decides how mechanics get explained, not a mechanic itself.
features.evidence: Every mechanic resolves to a moment or a written waiver.

features.name: Teaching tips (the mechanism)
features.mustUnderstand: Catalogs the persistent-hover-tip delivery mechanism; the mechanics the tips explain (par, strain, ram, threat tier, boost bays) are already covered under their own entries.
features.evidence: Persistent hover explainers. **A tip is reference you want again.**

features.name: Teaching waivers bookkeeping
features.mustUnderstand: Bookkeeping for which inventory rows are deliberately untaught and why; documents the teaching system's own decisions, not a mechanic.
features.evidence: A waiver is a **written decision not to teach something**, with a reason.

features.name: The tutorial (design intent)
features.mustUnderstand: Describes the tutorial's own design intent and build gate (unwinnable by construction, 0-of-200 sim requirement); the four verbs it teaches are already covered individually under rotate, scan, defend and attack.
features.evidence: The opening dive. **Unwinnable by construction**, and it must prove it 200 times before any deploy.

features.name: Tutorial beats (the mechanism)
features.mustUnderstand: Catalogs the scripted opening-dive beat ladder and its ordering rule; the verbs it teaches are already covered elsewhere, and the beat mechanism itself is dev-facing.
features.evidence: Beats are how the tutorial teaches, because coachmarks are gated off day 0 by `notBeforeDay: 1`.
